name: MonarchAvatar
title: Avatar
wrapsNative: AsyncImage (through MonarchRemoteImage) or Image, clipped to a RoundedRectangle, with a Text or SF Symbol fallback; HStack with negative spacing for MonarchAvatarGroup
summary: A picture of a person or an entity, with initials or a symbol as the fallback, an optional presence dot, and an overlapping group with a "+N" tile.
whenToUse: Wherever a person or an organisation is shown: list rows, comments, assignees, account menus, workspace switchers. Use MonarchAvatarGroup for several people in a small space.
whenNotToUse: For a website or app icon, use MonarchFavicon. For a presence without a picture, use MonarchPresenceDot. For uploading a new picture, use an avatar upload control.
api: init(image: Image?, name: String, seed: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, status: MonarchPresenceStatus? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false, statusLabel: String? = nil)

init(url: URL?, name: String, seed: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, status: MonarchPresenceStatus? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false, statusLabel: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAvatarSize { case xs, sm, md, lg, xl }

MonarchAvatarGroup.init(_ label: String, _ data: Data, id: KeyPath<Data.Element, ID>, maxVisible: Int? = nil, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, overflowLabel: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content)

MonarchAvatarGroup.init(_ label: String, _ data: Data, maxVisible: Int? = nil, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, overflowLabel: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content) where Data.Element: Identifiable

MonarchAvatarGroup.init(_ data: Data, id: KeyPath<Data.Element, ID>, maxVisible: Int? = nil, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, overflowLabel: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content)

MonarchAvatarGroup.init(_ data: Data, maxVisible: Int? = nil, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, shape: MonarchAvatarShape = .circle, overflowLabel: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Data.Element) -> Content) where Data.Element: Identifiable

options.name: image / url
options.description: The picture, from the app or loaded with AsyncImage. nil shows the fallback, which also shows while loading and after a failure.

options.name: name
options.description: The person or entity. Read by VoiceOver and used for the initials.

options.name: seed
options.description: Picks the fallback colour; the name by default. Pass a stable id so a renamed person keeps their colour.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: An SF Symbol shown instead of the initials, for entities without a logo.

options.name: shape
options.description: circle for people, square (rounded) for workspaces, organisations and brands.

options.name: size
options.description: xs (20), sm (24), md (32), lg (40) or xl (56) points before Dynamic Type.

options.name: status
options.description: A MonarchPresenceDot at the bottom trailing corner; its name is added to the spoken name.

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the avatar from VoiceOver when the name is written next to it.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the presence.

options.name: label (group)
options.description: Names the group for VoiceOver. Optional: without it the group is read as the number of people ("4 people").

options.name: maxVisible (group)
options.description: Show at most this many avatars, then a "+N" tile. With exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: overflowLabel (group)
options.description: Replaces the spoken "N more" of the tile.

states.name: initials
states.description: No picture, loading or failed: one or two initials on a subtle colour picked from the seed, in the strong colour of the same family.

states.name: symbol
states.description: With systemImage, or when the name has no letter or digit: the symbol (a person by default) on the same colours.

states.name: presence
states.description: A presence dot with a surface-coloured ring at the bottom trailing corner.

states.name: group overflow
states.description: A "+N" tile in the muted colours after the shown avatars, each ringed in the surface colour.

appearance: Fallback colours are five subtle-and-strong pairs of theme roles (accent, info, success, warning, AI), so they follow dark and both high-contrast themes; danger is left out so no face reads as an error. The square shape uses 6-point corners at sm and 8-point corners above. In a group each avatar is ringed with the surface colour and covers a quarter of the previous one.
platformNotes: The web derives a soft colour from a hue per name (or one of five data colours with palette="tokens"); iOS has no data colour roles, so it always uses five theme role pairs, picked with the same hash as the web so a seed lands on the same index. The web's xs and xl sizes and any number of pixels are not offered: Monarch's touch vocabulary is sm, md and lg, and a larger picture in a profile header can be an Image clipped by the app. The presence uses MonarchPresenceStatus, which adds do not disturb to the web's four. AvatarGroup on the web counts its children; SwiftUI cannot count view builder children on iOS 17, so the group takes the data and a content closure. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The avatar is one element with the image trait, named by the name, and by the presence when there is one ("Ana Silva, Online"); the name is built by a tested pure function.
The presence dot is not read on its own, and its form (bar, ring, half, square) keeps presence distinct without colour.
isDecorative hides the avatar from VoiceOver when the name is written beside it.
The group is a container named by its label; each avatar is read by its own name, then the tile as "2 more".
The avatar and its initials scale with Dynamic Type; initials shrink to fit rather than being cut.
edgeCases: An empty name or one made only of emoji shows the person symbol; the spoken name is the name as given.
Initials keep whole characters, so an emoji or an accented letter is never cut in half.
A URL that fails to load shows the fallback; a failure is not an error state.
In a group, give each avatar the same size and shape as the group; the group uses them for the overlap, the ring and the tile.
